column5: Equations (1)-(3), Tables 1-3, use R=461.51805 J/(kg K), TR=10 K, Ta=593 K, and Tb=232 K. Density is rho0=1/v0 from Eq. The enthalpy reference is exactly the additive convention inherited from Eq. (1) coefficients; this source does not establish h=0 at 273.15 K or a phase-transition reference. All retained states are stable liquid at p0: 283.15-353.15 K lies above approximately 273.15 K freezing and below approximately 372.76 K boiling stated by the release. The source reports stable-region relative uncertainty 0.0001 percent for density and 0.1 percent for cp0, and no separate h0 uncertainty. It says these may be considered estimates of standard uncertainty with coverage factor k=2, but supplies no probability distribution or confidence level; no confidence is inferred here. Each 5 K linear engineering curve has 15 Decimal80 evaluated knots rounded to 15 significant digits. Against its source equation at 99 interior probes per interval, maximum relative discrepancy is 0.00392514 percent for density, 0.00787327 percent for cp0, and 0.00795566 percent for h0; these engineering interpolation discrepancies are separate from source uncertainty and are not certified global bounds. The independently linear h0 and cp0 curves do not exactly preserve dh0/dT=cp0: maximum absolute derivative discrepancy is 3.51809610 J/(kg K), and maximum interval difference between delta-h0 and integral of linear cp0 is 1.09986894 J/kg (0.00524794 percent of delta-h0), both on 283.15-288.15 K.
